“He promised to donate half a million dollars to build in Kfar Chabad,” Rabbi Parshan, an askan from Toronto, was saying.

“I meant a quarter of a million,” said Mr. Tanenbaum, the donor.

The Rebbe responded, “Why are you scared to commit to half a million if Hashem can make you richer? Rabbi Parshan says you can give half a million…”

Mommy couldn’t believe it. Mr. Khazanski was a donor from Toronto too! She told Tatty, who immediately sent the video link to Mr. Khazanski.

My wife saw this right after asking for a bracha for you at the Ohel, he wrote. Surely, committing to help before your business deals work out will be the vessel for Hashem’s blessing.

Mr. Khazanski responded immediately, Okay. Start planning the new Chabad House. I will pay all the rent.

Before Lag B’omer, Mr. Khazanski saw tremendous brachos for his business. Not only did a difficult deal in Nigeria work out, but he also unexpectedly received another deal in a totally different industry—and made a lot of money!

We immediately signed a contract for a house and opened up our beautiful Beis Chabad. Since then, we have moved to an even bigger house, where we have a shul, a preschool, and a kosher store. Until today, Mr. Khazanski helps pay the rent, all because of the bracha he got from the Rebbe.

We feel blessed to have received a personal sign from the Rebbe that Nigeria is definitely our makom hashlichus!

Our apartment was too small to host. How could we continue our shlichus?

Most Chabad Houses don’t start off in fancy mansions—but ours did.

You see, when our family moved on shlichus to Lagos, Nigeria, an elderly Yid offered us his mansion to use as our home and Chabad House. But soon, we had to move.

We settled in a bigger city, Abuja, and lived in a much smaller apartment. Pretty soon, we realized we needed a bigger home for our shlichus.

But finding one wasn’t easy. Nigeria is a poor African country, and many homes don’t have running water and electricity. Also, even if we found a proper house, most owners wanted two years of rent payments before moving in!

Left without a Chabad House, my parents began doubting if Africa was the right place for their shlichus. Should we leave Nigeria? They wondered sadly.

Unsure of what to do, they decided to ask the Rebbe.

Just in time for Chof Beis Shvat, we flew to New York to visit the Ohel. Tatty and Mommy wrote to the Rebbe, describing the situation and asking what to do.

A few days later, while still in New York, Tatty heard about Mr. Khazanski, a businessman in Toronto with several business deals in Nigeria. Tatty arranged a meeting with him for 6:00 p.m. that day and quickly booked a flight to Canada.

At the meeting, Tatty and Mr. Khazanski discussed the Chabad House in Nigeria for a long time.

“I’m truly amazed by your shlichus,” said Mr. Khazanski. “However, I’m in the middle of too many business deals right now. As soon as they work out, I will certainly help you. Can you ask the Rebbe for a blessing that I should be successful?”

“Of course,” Tatty promised. That night, back at the Ohel, he wrote another long letter
